title: Ceiling fan light flickers when fan is used
reported_symptom: I have a double-gang box with a Leviton dimmer switch , a Lutron fan switch , and ran 14/3 to a Hunter 53408 ceiling fan . I wired everything up and the controls work well, independently; the Leviton dims the T12 3.5W LED bulbs and the Lutron adjusts the fan from low to medium to high. When both are turned on and I adjust the Lutron speed, the bulbs will sporadically flicker off and on. This does not happen every single time but there's a 50% chance that a flicker occurs when adjusting the fan speed. Do I have a hardware incompatibility? One guess is that the Lutron is causing some weird fluctuation on the neutral but I'm no expert. My second guess is that the leads for the fan versus light is not adequately separated inside the fan housing. Per request, below is a wiring diagram. I made it from memory so if something looks off then please request clarity. Update 1: Adjusting the ceiling fan speed will sometimes make the ceiling light stay on at full brightness after flickering. Turning the Lutron on or off also affects the behavior of the light. The flicker will also affect a dimmer+light on the same circuit in an adjacent hallway. Same Leviton dimmer but this has a Great Value bulb. This light always returns to normal after a flicker. Update 2: Leaving the Lutron on high and using the pull strings on the fan causes zero issues for the bulbs. There is another light on the same circuit which is not dimmable and it experiences zero flicker.
author: MonkeyZeus

title: Help with lights flickering at weird regular interval
reported_symptom:

The video starts with the 23 second "normal" period, followed by 17 seconds of flickering, and shows 2 cycles. May need to turn screen brightness up, but if you watch closely the flashes are evident. Context about my home's electrical system: video is of ceiling light flickering is not isolated to a single circuit. Occurs in bedroom
circuit, bathroom circuit, kitchen circuit (fridge light),
outside garage light, and floor lamps plugged into outlets 1950's house, copper wiring, no ground on most circuits except for
kitchen. Both dimmer switch and LED claim compatibility with dimming functionality. Oddly enough, this light doesn't flicker, at least not strongly enough that I can perceive it 100 amp service Things I've tried already: Had utility company replace connections to weather-head due to
imbalance on legs of main coming into panel. Flickering was occurring

could have poor connection, but flickering continued. Inspected panel for any loose connections at bus bar, tightened a few, but found nothing suspect I'm fairly handy, an engineer, and confident in my ability to troubleshoot without getting myself electrocuted, but I'm out of ideas. title: Light working after washing machine has run
reported_symptom:
An electrician has looked at this and said it is legal because it was up to code when it was made. But if changes are done to it, it must be up to the current code. I will have it fixed by the same electrician, but I want to understand how the following can happen.
He also told me a bit about the wiring which I have illustrated here. The switch at C turns on the lamp in the ceiling E. The switch at D can turn on an additional lamp, but nothing is currently hooked up to that outlet. The switches at A and B each turn on the outlet under them. Everything was working as it should. I hooked up a few things at A and B (such as a vacuum cleaner). Everything was still working fine. I hooked up a charger for a laptop at B. The light at E flashed on and off for a few seconds and then turned off. I thought it was the bulb, but that was not the case (I have checked that several times - the issue is never the bulb).
The situation - neither A, B or E is working. I checked and could see some current was flowing when I switched them on, but I don't have the tools to see how much. I left the switch at C turned on even though it had no effect. Suddenly, the lamp at E worked again. C could be turned on and off and it worked as expected. I was puzzled. Stupid as I was, I plugged something into A again. E stopped working again. I left C turned on again hoping it would start working again. Suddenly, the light turned on. I noticed it turned on while the washing machine was running at its loudest. Once the washing machine stopped, E turned off again. This pattern repeated two more times. The fourth time, C worked again without the need for the washing machine being on. Even more puzzled I decided not to touch A or B since I now had working light at E. However, I had to turn off F to do work on something else. Once again E has stopped working, still has some current running through it. It no longer seems to be effected by the washing machine. I have checked all the places I can and there is no loose connections. I cannot figure out how all this is effecting each other, and I am quite puzzled by it. How can this be?
I can add further explanations and pictures if that is needed.

title: Washing Machine door locking/lights working, but no power to solenoid or motor
reported_symptom:
My machine is turning on with the led's lighting, allowing me to select and start a program, doors locking and then the counter starts to countdown as normal. But nothing else happens, no water and no motor. I have tried spin modes etc, but they are all the same. I have checked that the solenoids work when powered from an external source, But they are not receiving power from the control unit.
There is still meat on the motor bushes and the drum spins freely. This is my first time looking at fixing a washing machine so I don't really know what else I can check, If there are fusees or other safety 'trips' etc? That said, I would have thought that if that was the issue there would be an Error message showing? is there maybe a relay I can replace? or..? Any help would be greatly appreciated! Ash Machine: Electrolux / Zanussi ZWF12280W EDIT: inspired by jwh20's comment bellow, I took a closer look at the control board. I think it might be something to do with the 'chard' section.
